- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast lows by 5–10% to capture downside risk.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward sentiment spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to peak forecasts.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >15% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–8%.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., +0.33 → -0.33), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- Forecasting horizon 30d is prone to overconfidence in early days; cap forecast at 10% below 30-day moving average if sentiment is neutral or declining.
